passages.provision_quote: On or before January 1, 2026, a municipality with a population of seventy-five thousand persons or more must authorize by ordinance and incorporate into its development regulations, zoning regulations and other official controls the development of duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes and townhomes as a permitted use on both of the following:
passages.note: Chaptered text of the instrument Gowan voted on; it names no voter, so actor and tally fields are null here.

rows.reasoning: Gowan voted Aye on HB 2721 (2024), a single-subject law forcing larger municipalities to permit duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes and townhomes and barring them from imposing more restrictive permitting, floor-area, owner-occupancy or parking requirements on them. That removes local zoning limits that block private building, so it is on-question for "at most, cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building", but one deregulation vote cannot show he would do nothing more, which is what "Rely on the market to set prices and supply" requires. It also fails "set binding rules on the private market like rent caps or required affordable units" (the bill binds municipalities, not private owners) and names no subsidies or tax breaks, so no rung is matched clause for clause.
